## kb_to_source

Every normative sentence of the 50 documents was traced to a source atom. Restatements found and judged derivable (not additions): "four-tire set and a five-tire set … charged alike for one fitted tire" (from "for the one tire fitted"); "how the member pays for any later Tire Center charge is not [read]" (from "primary tender of the tires' purchase"); "not any other membership the member holds" (from "membership whose card was presented"); "read from the system's records … not from the member's account" (evidence_contract authority system_record); "a request for another tire size or another appointment date for that vehicle is still a new set" (dedup distinct_fields); package-schedule comparison bullets (pure parameter comparisons).

Additions / rewrites / omissions: none found.

Prerequisite-side specific checks:
- Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …", a resolving tool named beside a sentence): none. Each of the five discoverable tool names occurs only in its own hub's invocation block.
- A task's opening world state written in as a policy fact: none. Worked figures are labelled hypothetical and use values that are not any task's records (the one date coincidence — "today is 2026-10-05" in `rotation_repeat_visit_rates` — illustrates a rotation loyalty count with invented charge dates and carries no task-0 record).

## bijection_verdict

**PASS** — every normative atom of the three extended policies (baselines, all 15 factor ladders in full, both prerequisites, overwrites) and of the base policies governing their subjects is entailed by the tire corpus at the same strength; the retired surface is borne and marked; no unsourced normative claim. First revision; no previous revision exists.

Policy-side notes (do not change this verdict):
1. The overwrite of `tire_installation_charges` ("a tpms_service_kit entry … for each wheel with a pressure sensor when that fee is not zero") is declared by `tire_ext_flat_repair_charge`, whose replaced_by text concerns the flat-repair entry and itself says "any fee that no rule folds into another entry, such as the sensor kits charged when a set is installed, remains a separate entry at its own fee". After the retirement no in-force rule books the installation-day sensor kit, while the replacement text presumes such kits are still charged. The KB renders both faithfully (`installation_day_charges` item 3 retired; `repeat_flat_repair_work_charge` "One entry for the wheel"), so the incoherence is source-side, not a rendering defect.
2. `lifetime_rotation_included` / `lifetime_rebalance_included` / `flat_repair_included` remain as parameters ("included for life: yes" in `lifetime_service_entitlements`) although the clauses giving them effect are retired; on packages whose flat repair fee is 0 but sensor kit fee is not, the current flat-repair work method still yields a non-zero repeat-repair charge. Source-side; the KB carries the parameters as the source has them.
